Dongfeng TE46 4x2 Electric Tractor for Port and Short-Haul Routes

A route-first review of catalogue configuration, port duty cycles, charging, trailer fit and procurement checks for the TE46.

TE46 position and verified configuration

The Dongfeng catalogue lists TE46 in a paired TE46 / TE4Z row as a 4x2 electric tractor in the 42 t gross combination weight class. That row specifies a CATL 400 kWh battery, LvKong motor output of 315 kW rated and 510 kW peak, a 4AMT transmission, and dual-gun charging at 500 A. These are the published family-row values available for screening. The row groups two model names, so a buyer should not assume that every listed choice or detail is identical on an individual vehicle.

The same row groups GB and EU charging interfaces and shows paired axle and wheelbase entries without assigning every value to one badge. Ask for the exact model code, connector, axle, ratio and dimensions on a signed, vehicle-specific schedule. A catalogue summary does not establish a delivered vehicle's payload, homologation, operating range or charging duration. Those facts must come from the selected configuration and destination-market documents.

Map the route before deciding it is a port tractor

A 4x2 tractor can be a candidate for port, plant and short regional work when the trailer combination, road surface and traction requirement fit the approved configuration. Start by recording loaded and empty legs, trailer type, actual gross combination weight, distance per loop, gradients, queue time, road condition and operating hours. Include gate queues, crane alignment, loading, inspection and coupling because stationary time affects dispatch capacity even when it adds no kilometres.

Separate a controlled shuttle from a route that only begins at a port. A repeatable yard-to-depot loop may have predictable returns and planned dwell; a mixed route with public-road segments, variable trailers, steep ramps or changing payloads needs a different assessment. Review the most demanding regular segment, not just an easy loop. Check swept path, coupling space, ramp transitions, surface grip and clearance with the actual trailer. A 4x2 layout alone does not prove suitability for any particular site.

Build an energy record from real shifts

Battery capacity is not a range promise. To assess whether the listed 400 kWh option covers the operation, collect data from a comparable vehicle or a controlled pilot. Record distance, payload or gross combination weight, speed, temperature, elevation, waiting, accessory use, state of charge at dispatch and return, and charging energy delivered. Keep loaded and empty legs separate where possible. A short demonstration lap or fleet-wide average can hide the demanding shift that determines whether the vehicle returns with enough reserve.

Use the record to set an operating reserve for the next dispatch, diversions and seasonal conditions. Do not plan to use every indicated kilowatt-hour on the normal route. If the energy requirement leaves too little margin, review the route, charging opportunities, battery choice or tractor class. The electric tractor charging guide explains how to assemble a depot plan; its capacity examples are not measured TE46 range data.

Schedule charging around terminal shifts

The listed 500 A figure is current, not a guaranteed charging power or duration. Actual power depends on pack voltage, charger capability, the vehicle's acceptance limits, state of charge, temperature and site constraints. Ask the vehicle supplier and charger provider to confirm connector, voltage range, current limits, vehicle charge acceptance and whether the stated current applies per gun or to the combined arrangement. Validate any time estimate against the selected truck and charger.

Draw the dispatch schedule beside the charging schedule. Include arrival variation, queuing, coupling, loading, inspections, breaks and cleaning. If several vehicles return together, simultaneous charging can create a site peak; managed staggering may be more useful than adding equipment without checking the electrical supply. Have a qualified electrical designer review the depot load, transformer capacity, protection, cable routing and future fleet size. NREL's medium- and heavy-duty vehicle analysis discusses grid impacts and managed charging; its findings are planning evidence, not a promise about a particular depot.

Check the terminal interface and tractor-trailer combination

A port deployment has physical interfaces a catalogue table cannot settle. Confirm fifth-wheel height and position, kingpin compatibility, trailer brake and electrical connections, charging inlet access, cable reach in the parking layout, and safe separation between charging equipment and vehicle movement. Ensure a charging bay does not obstruct fire access, crane traffic, pedestrian paths or emergency egress. Review terminal operating rules and the vehicle's approved use for the destination market.

Confirm axle loads, tyre specification, permitted combination mass, gradeability for the intended route and braking configuration on the vehicle-specific sheet. The catalogue's 42 t figure is a GCW class, not a claim that every trailer and load may legally operate at that mass in every jurisdiction. The broader Dongfeng tractor selection guide covers other classes; use it alongside local legal review and the final homologation documents.

Know the limits and run a disciplined pilot

The available data does not provide verified TE46 range, energy consumption per kilometre, battery warranty, purchase price, charging duration, gradeability or payload for a named export market. Do not fill these gaps with another TE model's values or an online estimate. The grouped TE46 / TE4Z row also leaves some model-specific details unresolved. Request a current signed specification for the exact model code, market, connector, axle, wheelbase and options before comparing bids.

A pilot should represent a normal difficult shift rather than a demonstration lap. Agree the route, load, measurement method, charging access, downtime logging and success criteria before dispatch. Track completed trips, energy per trip, charging dwell, queue time, driver feedback, availability and maintenance findings. Compare those results with the actual baseline operation. If the pilot's route, trailer or load differs from the intended deployment, label the difference rather than extrapolating the result to the whole fleet.

Buyer checklist for a TE46 quotation

Send the destination country, quantity, driving-side requirement, trailer drawings, target gross combination weight, payload, route map, loaded distance, empty return, grades, surface, hours per shift, shifts per day, ambient temperature and terminal dwell windows. Add available site supply, charger connector and rated output, simultaneous charging expectations, and terminal access or noise requirements. These inputs let the configuration discussion begin with the real duty cycle rather than a generic product description.

Ask for an exact model code and signed schedule resolving the shared catalogue row: battery variant, motor output, transmission, axle model and ratio, wheelbase, tyres, charging connector and current limit, safety equipment, weights, dimensions and market approval. Confirm delivery scope, training, diagnostics, service arrangements and spare-parts support in writing. The electric tractor product page lists the current family information; use the contact page to request a configuration review.

Frequently asked questions

What configuration does the catalogue list for the TE46?

The shared TE46 / TE4Z row lists 4x2, 42 t GCW, CATL 400 kWh, 315 kW rated / 510 kW peak motor output, 4AMT and dual-gun 500 A. Confirm exact connector and chassis details on the selected model's specification.

Can a TE46 work on a port shuttle route?

It may be considered when the approved combination mass, traction, route, turning space and charging plan fit the job. Check ramp conditions, trailer geometry and local rules before selecting it.

Does 400 kWh establish the truck's range?

No. Range depends on route, operating mass, speed, grade, temperature, auxiliary loads and usable energy. Use representative measurements and keep an operating reserve.

What should buyers verify before ordering?

Request a signed, model-specific build sheet, connector confirmation, vehicle weights and dimensions, market approval, charging limits, warranty terms and service scope.

Discuss the route and configuration

Send the country, trailer, payload or GCW, daily distance, grades, shift pattern and charging conditions for a configuration review.
